ops.title: Phase-1 coordination: cross-lane contracts + open-question rulings for P1b/P1c/P1d
ops.body:
Orchestrator rulings on the P1 specs' open questions (cut/p1/SPEC-P1{b,c,d}-*.md). These bind the
P1 implementation lanes. All within the approved "break v1 in place, broken module, CI dark until
phase 3" structure.

AUDIT-TOKEN CONTRACT (P1b Q3 / P1c 4.1): internal/proc KEEPS `AuditToken [32]byte` +
AuditTokenFromBytes/PID/PIDVersion/Valid exported -- it is a transport value read off a socket,
not a process identity, so it stays exported even though identity collapses to an unexported
struct. internal/proc DROPS the signaling variant (proc_signal_with_audittoken -- no caller in the
new design; Stopped.Reap observes, never signals). internal/trust imports internal/proc for
AuditToken and nothing else; internal/proc must NOT import internal/trust.

PEER DELETION (P1c OQ6) -> option (a): delete `peer` wholesale in phase 1. peer.Identity refs in
internal/runtimeauth/capability.go:12, daemon/child_fence.go:12, wire/stop_prepare.go:13, and the
trust.PeerRole / SignatureDigest uses in daemon/child_fence.go:145-160,299-306 DANGLE -- they are
in wire(P2)/daemon(P3) packages already slated for rewrite, so they join the broken set. Phase-1
gate is `scripts/test.sh ./internal/...`, not whole-module compile.

P1e IS SUBSUMED, not a standalone phase-1 code lane. "One comparison site" = internal/proc owns
the sole unexported `matches`. The outside sites (daemon/child_fence.go:312, service/
stop_runtime.go:322) are in packages rewritten in P2/P3 and delegate to internal/proc's operations
THEN (internal/proc exposes the operation, never an exported comparison for callers to open-code);
peer/peer.go:26-30 vanishes with peer's deletion. Phase 1 leaves those packages broken (expected).

ROLES (P1c OQ7): P1c deletes trust's role/authority machinery (spec 3.5). wire (P2) rebuilds the
{Control, Business} lanes per DESIGN 2; DESIGN I25's per-role capacity-1 reservation is restated
over those two lanes in P2. Not phase-1's concern.

LOW-STAKES RULINGS: PolicyDigest stays [32]byte (OQ4 a; amend DESIGN 2 L160). Verify takes
*Requirement by pointer (OQ5 a; a value+bool would silently downgrade a daemon to UID-only).
Legacy bbolt sweep -> transitional `Daemon.LegacyStores []string` carrying the sweep's
deletion-release TODO (P1b Q2 a). P1d interim entry -> root `Run(ctx, *internal/proc.Owner, Cmd)`,
exported-but-externally-uncallable (internal param type), unexported at P3 (P1d Q1 a).

DEFERRED TO PHASE 4 (consumer migration; do NOT block P1): consumer-owned flock landing (P1b Q1 --
synckit/cc-interact/cc-notes/reposync use the lock for their own files; lean toward a thin public
re-export of internal/flock preserving the ErrLockBusy identity, decide at flag-day). CloseInheritedFDs
residue (P1b Q4). Off-disk consumer re-verification (fusekit/cc-pool/cookiesync) -- export census is
the backstop.

TRUST IS T0+T1, NOT PURE KERNEL-ONLY (per note 275d06d + cut/seccode/DESIGN-REVIEW.md): P1c builds
the five T0 reads (require CS_VALID explicitly; keep csposture's CS_DEBUGGED clause) PLUS T1 -- a
sixth read of CS_OPS_BLOB: find the CD whose SHA-256[0:20]==CS_OPS_CDHASH, resolve the CMS
SignerInfo-designated leaf (via issuerAndSerialNumber/SKI, NEVER "the cert with the matching OU"),
x509.ParseCertificate it, assert leaf.Subject.OU == CD teamID == req.TeamID + the Developer ID OID
markers. Closes the verifySignature() silent-skip-on-OU-less-leaf hole (DESIGN-REVIEW 3, 9.2, 10.5).
DROP the DECISION 7 cdhash-memo SecCode fallback. T2 (self-verify CMS) NOT in phase 1. DER op-16
grammar (OQ1/OQ2) + status-word entitlement bits (OQ3) to be MEASURED inline (cert on hand) before
P1c dispatch, not guessed.
